# netbox_cluster_type (Resource)

From the [official documentation](https://docs.netbox.dev/en/stable/features/virtualization/#cluster-types):

> A cluster type represents a technology or mechanism by which a cluster is formed. For example, you might create a cluster type named "VMware vSphere" for a locally hosted cluster or "DigitalOcean NYC3" for one hosted by a cloud provider.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netbox_cluster_type" "vmw_vsphere" {
  name = "VMware vSphere 6"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the cluster type.

### Optional

- `comments` (String) Free-form comments about the cluster type. Needs NetBox 4.5.0 or later.
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values of the object, as a map of field name to value.
- `description` (String) A description of the cluster type.
- `owner_id` (Number) The ID of the owner associated with the cluster type. Needs NetBox 4.5.0 or later.
- `slug` (String) The URL-friendly slug of the cluster type.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags assigned to the object, by name.

### Read-Only

- `cluster_count` (Number) The number of cluster objects that refer to the cluster type.
- `created` (String) When the cluster type was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_updated` (String) When the cluster type was last changed.
- `tags_all` (Set of String) All tags assigned to the object, including those not managed by Terraform.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the numeric NetBox ID of the object
terraform import netbox_cluster_type.example 1
```
